# Known intentional Redis compatibility divergences.
#
# Format:
# <suite/test/command> :: <reason-category> :: <short reason>
#
# Reason categories:
# - feature-killed-per-A.11
# - mako-design-difference
# - mako-correctness-fix
#
KEYS/SCAN/DBSIZE set visibility :: mako-design-difference :: Set members are stored as hidden length-prefixed composite keys outside the visible `table_key_` namespace. Exposing set logical keys through keyspace enumeration needs a shared logical-key index or safe remote-scan design, not a local composite-prefix scan.
KEYS/SCAN/DBSIZE list visibility :: mako-design-difference :: Lists are stored as hidden meta/element composite keys outside the visible `table_key_` namespace. Exposing list logical keys through keyspace enumeration needs a shared logical-key index or safe remote-scan design, not a local composite-prefix scan.
KEYS/SCAN/DBSIZE sorted-set visibility :: mako-design-difference :: Sorted sets are stored as hidden member/score/meta composite keys outside the visible `table_key_` namespace. Exposing zset logical keys through keyspace enumeration needs a shared logical-key index or safe remote-scan design, not a local composite-prefix scan.
makoConMultiTrd extended Redis commands :: mako-design-difference :: Project decision: keep the alternate MultiTrd binary ABI-compatible only. Redis correctness is claimed for `third-party/redis/cpp/makoCon.cc`; making MultiTrd a correctness target would require executor deduplication and is not needed for this PR.
FLUSHDB/FLUSHALL :: mako-design-difference :: Project decision: Mako Redis remains a single-keyspace server. `SELECT 0` is supported for client compatibility, but Redis logical DB selection is not mapped onto Mako DB namespaces; `FLUSHDB`/`FLUSHALL` clear the single Mako Redis keyspace.
BITOP destination type :: mako-design-difference :: BITOP writes its result only when the destination is absent or a string; a destination holding another type returns WRONGTYPE instead of being overwritten as Redis does. Overwriting would need the SET path's collection-replacement logic in the executor.
OBJECT ENCODING/REFCOUNT :: mako-design-difference :: Mako stores no Redis object encodings or refcounts. OBJECT ENCODING reports the canonical large-object encoding per type (raw, quicklist, hashtable, skiplist) and REFCOUNT is always 1; FREQ and IDLETIME return errors because access time is not tracked.
MEMORY USAGE :: mako-design-difference :: Reported as key bytes + serialized value bytes + a fixed per-key overhead, in the spirit of Redis's estimate; SAMPLES is accepted and ignored.
RESTORE hash payload :: mako-design-difference :: Restoring a hash payload merges into an existing hash at the key (pre-existing behavior). String, set, and sorted-set payloads replace the key. REPLACE is accepted but the BUSYKEY check is not performed.
SPUBLISH/SSUBSCRIBE :: mako-design-difference :: Sharded Pub/Sub is served from the same single-keyspace registry as classic Pub/Sub, so it is correct only within one makoCon process, like classic Pub/Sub.
SLOWLOG/LATENCY/ACL :: mako-design-difference :: Compatibility shims for monitoring tools and client libraries: SLOWLOG and LATENCY report empty data, and ACL exposes a single implicit 'default' user that cannot be modified.
